---
title: "Aligning rounds"
---

Alignment is the step that makes cyclic IF possible. Between rounds the plate
is removed, stripped, re-stained and re-imaged, so the field of view shifts.
Registration recovers that shift, so a nucleus can be followed across rounds.

## align_plates.py

```bash
python bin/align_plates.py 4126 4127 4128 [options]
```

The first ID is the **reference**; the others are registered onto it.

Alignment is computed on a nuclear channel — DAPI by default, because it is
present in every round and, unlike an antibody stain, marks the same structure
each time.

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--channel NAME` | `DAPI` | Channel used for registration |
| `-n N` | 5 | Number of alignments averaged |
| `--sample-alignments` | off | Per-sample alignments instead of a fixed number |
| `--threshold N` | 100 | Distance threshold for accepting an alignment |
| `--tolerance N` | 10 | Allowed distance from the alignment centroid |
| `--iqr N` | 1.5 | Inter-quartile-range factor for outlier removal (0 disables) |
| `--gallery N` | 4 | Size of the alignment gallery grid |
| `--seed N` | random | Random seed for sampling |
| `--env NAME` | — | Environment file to load |

### Choosing the parameters

`--threshold` and `--tolerance` control how tolerant the matching is. Raising
the threshold accepts larger shifts between rounds; lowering the tolerance
demands that individual alignments agree more closely with their consensus.

`--iqr` removes outlying alignments before averaging. Set it to `0` to keep
every alignment, which is worth doing once when diagnosing a plate that will
not register.

`--gallery` writes a visual grid of alignments back to OMERO. Look at it — a
registration that is numerically plausible but visually wrong is the failure
mode you most want to catch early.

## Filling in missing masks

Secondary rounds are often segmented on the nucleus alone, so they carry no
cell masks. This regenerates them using the alignment from the reference:

```bash
python bin/create_masks.py 4127
```

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--sample-alignments` | off | Use per-sample rather than per-well alignments |
| `--force` | off | Replace masks that already exist |
| `--env NAME` | — | Environment file to load |

`--force` is the flag to reach for after changing alignment parameters —
without it, masks already present are left untouched, and you would silently
be aggregating against the old registration.
